record.title: Insilico reports preliminary Phase 1 activity for AI-designed pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331
record.summary: Insilico Medicine reported preliminary Phase 1 results for ISM6331, an investigational pan-TEAD inhibitor designed using its Chemistry42 generative-AI platform. In the company’s 26 October release, it reported a 40.0% ORR at 130 mg among two of five response-evaluable mesothelioma participants, and an 18.2% ORR across 30–130 mg among four of 22 participants. The company reported 36 enrolled participants and ongoing dose escalation at an August 14 data cutoff. These are issuer-reported early-phase results from small denominators; controlled efficacy, independent interpretation and any causal contribution from AI are not established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Insilico Medicine announced on 26 October 2026 that it presented preliminary first-in-human Phase 1 results for the investigational oral pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331 at the 2026 ESMO Congress; the company says the molecule was designed using its Chemistry42 generative-AI platform.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The company reports a 40.0% objective response rate at 130 mg once daily among two of five response-evaluable mesothelioma participants; across 30–130 mg, it reports an 18.2% ORR (four of 22 response-evaluable participants) and 68.2% disease control rate.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The company says 36 participants were enrolled across 15–130 mg as of the 14 August 2026 data cutoff, with dose escalation ongoing; it reports no dose-limiting toxicities through 130 mg and Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events in 8.3% of participants.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The issuer release does not establish controlled efficacy, comparative benefit, independent clinical interpretation, regulatory approval or that use of generative AI caused the reported clinical outcomes.

evidence_gaps.description: The ESMO abstract/presentation and current ClinicalTrials.gov record were not inspected; the release is the sole source for cohort-level results in this activation.
Response and safety figures are issuer-reported from an ongoing, uncontrolled Phase 1 trial with small response-evaluable denominators.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported early clinical activity persists, a generative-AI-designed small molecule reaching measurable human antitumor responses could materially inform AI-enabled drug discovery and TEAD-inhibitor development. The evidence is an issuer report from a small ongoing Phase 1 study, not a controlled efficacy result or independent analysis.
limitations: All clinical outcome and safety figures in this review come from the issuer’s press release.
The 40.0% ORR at 130 mg is based on two responses among five response-evaluable participants; the across-dose ORR is four of 22.
The study is ongoing Phase 1 with no comparator arm; the data cutoff is 14 August 2026 and dose escalation was ongoing.
The release does not establish approval, comparative benefit or that AI caused the clinical response.
The ESMO presentation, abstract and registry were not independently inspected in this activation.
brief.summary: Insilico Medicine reported preliminary Phase 1 results for ISM6331, an investigational pan-TEAD inhibitor designed using its Chemistry42 generative-AI platform. In the company’s 26 October release, it reported a 40.0% ORR at 130 mg among two of five response-evaluable mesothelioma participants, and an 18.2% ORR across 30–130 mg among four of 22 participants. The company reported 36 enrolled participants and ongoing dose escalation at an August 14 data cutoff. These are issuer-reported early-phase results from small denominators; controlled efficacy, independent interpretation and any causal contribution from AI are not established.

technical.claimed_result: At 130 mg, 2 of 5 response-evaluable mesothelioma participants had a reported partial response (40.0% ORR); across 30–130 mg, 4 of 22 response-evaluable participants had a reported response (18.2% ORR) and DCR was 68.2%. The release reports N=36 enrolled, dose escalation ongoing at the 14 August 2026 data cutoff.
technical.demonstrated_result: Insilico publicly released the Phase 1 update and said it was presented at ESMO 2026. The reported clinical outcomes have not been independently assessed in this activation.
technical.implementation_status: Investigational Phase 1; dose escalation ongoing at data cutoff. Insilico said it planned to complete dose selection and, subject to emerging data, initiate a Phase 2a randomized dose-optimization study.
technical.mechanism: ISM6331 is described as an oral non-covalent pan-TEAD1–4 inhibitor designed and optimized using Chemistry42 generative AI; the Phase 1 study assesses safety, pharmacokinetics and preliminary antitumor activity.
technical.regime: Ongoing global multicenter open-label Phase 1 study NCT06566079 in advanced solid tumors; release focuses on heavily pretreated mesothelioma; data cutoff 14 August 2026.
technical.reproducibility: The release cites trial NCT06566079 and an ESMO presentation but the registry record, abstract and presentation materials were not inspected in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: No comparator arm or controlled efficacy baseline is reported in the issuer release.

brief.title: Insilico reports preliminary Phase 1 activity for AI-designed pan-TEAD inhibitor ISM6331
brief.why_it_matters: A first-in-human clinical response signal from a molecule described as AI-designed is relevant to the path from computational drug discovery to patient testing. The data are preliminary and based on small response-evaluable groups in an ongoing Phase 1 study; they do not establish comparative benefit, approval or that AI caused the outcome.
